    CHEERSafe Exposure Workflow¶

    This notebook runs the cheersafe.exposure chain end to end: a building inventory is mapped onto the structural archetype M and a seeded resistance configuration C, per-event wind and flood intensities are assigned from hazard control points to building centroids and converted to continuous hazard IDs (Wind_Tr, Flood_Tr), zone ids are attached, and the STARR-compatible export is written and read back.

    Every calculation is called explicitly and its return value assigned by the notebook, following the package's strict-return pattern. See the exposure manual for the methodology and the API reference for signatures.

    !!! warning "Execution profiles" Smoke mode (default) builds a realistic synthetic case with SyntheticExposureData (2,000 buildings, 5 events, EPSG:5070, the real 1 km grid origin) and runs in about 20 seconds with no external data.

    **Full mode** (`CHEERSAFE_EXPOSURE_SMOKE=0`) reads the Eastern North Carolina demo inventory
(2,000 points), the 97 `Old97` hazard layers (63,094 control points each) and the LEAPHI zone layer
from the `Loss Estimates` folder (`CHEERSAFE_EXPOSURE_DATA`). It needs about 200 MB of RAM and a
minute. Missing files are reported and the dependent cells are skipped.

    Plan¶

    1. Choose the execution profile and output folder.
    2. Load (or generate) the inventory, hazard layers and zones.
    3. Assign archetypes M and configurations C; inspect their distributions.
    4. Map hazard intensities to buildings and transform them to hazard IDs; compare Nearest and Inverse_d4.
    5. Assign zone ids.
    6. Write the STARR export and verify that the files align.

    Archetypes M and configurations C¶

    M (1-8) is deterministic from stories, roof shape and garage (Peng 2013, Table 3.1). C (1-192) is one row of ComponentCombination_All.json, drawn per building from the construction-period and coast-distance rules (Peng 2013, Tables 3.6-3.7) through the seeded Sampling stream, so a seed reproduces the draw.

    if data_available:
    exposure = Exposure(
        inventory_path=str(inventory_path),
        hazard_dir=str(hazard_dir),
        zones_path=str(zones_path),
        average_mode=AVERAGE_MODE,
        zone_id_col=ZONE_ID,
        coast_threshold_miles=COAST_THRESHOLD_MILES,
        drop_unmatched_occupancy=DROP_UNMATCHED_OCCUPANCY,
        seed=SMOKE_SEED,
    )

    Hazard mapping and hazard IDs¶

    Buildings are clipped to the control-point bounding box, matched to their nearest control points, and each event's wind (m/s) and flood (m) are assigned and converted to mph and inches before interpolation onto the package's discrete hazard IDs. Wind_Tr lies in [1, 25] and Flood_Tr in [1, 136].

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    if data_available:
    try:
        started = time.perf_counter()
        exposure.clipped_inventory = exposure.calculate_clipped_inventory(exposure.archetype_inventory)
        centroids = exposure.clipped_inventory.geometry.centroid
        building_xy = np.column_stack([centroids.x, centroids.y])
        k_neighbors = 1 if AVERAGE_MODE == "Nearest" else exposure.idw_neighbors
        exposure.neighbor_index, exposure.neighbor_distance = exposure.calculate_neighbor_match(
            building_xy, exposure.hazard_points_xy, k_neighbors
        )
        exposure.wind_ids, exposure.flood_ids = exposure.calculate_hazard_ids(
            exposure.neighbor_index, exposure.neighbor_distance, exposure.hazard_wind, exposure.hazard_flood
        )
        assert 1.0 <= exposure.wind_ids.min() and exposure.wind_ids.max() <= 25.0
        assert 1.0 <= exposure.flood_ids.min() and exposure.flood_ids.max() <= 136.0
        print(f"{len(exposure.clipped_inventory)} buildings inside the hazard bounds, {len(exposure.event_names)} events")
        print(f"Wind_Tr range {exposure.wind_ids.min():.3f}-{exposure.wind_ids.max():.3f}; "
              f"Flood_Tr range {exposure.flood_ids.min():.3f}-{exposure.flood_ids.max():.3f}; "
              f"{time.perf_counter() - started:.1f} s")
        # Compare the two averaging modes on the first event
        index_4, distance_4 = exposure.calculate_neighbor_match(building_xy, exposure.hazard_points_xy, 4)
        nearest_wind = exposure.calculate_event_intensity(exposure.hazard_wind[0], index_4, distance_4, mode="Nearest")
        idw_wind = exposure.calculate_event_intensity(exposure.hazard_wind[0], index_4, distance_4, mode="Inverse_d4")
        print(f"event {exposure.event_names[0]}: mean |Nearest - Inverse_d4| = {np.abs(nearest_wind - idw_wind).mean():.3f} m/s")
    except BaseException:
        restore_state()
        raise

    Zone assignment¶

    Each building takes the id of the zone polygon containing its centroid; buildings outside every zone get -1.

    exposure.zone_ids = exposure.calculate_zone_assignment(exposure.clipped_inventory, exposure.zones, ZONE_ID)
    zone_counts = pd.Series(exposure.zone_ids).value_counts().sort_index()
    print(f"{(exposure.zone_ids == -1).sum()} buildings outside every zone; {zone_counts[zone_counts.index != -1].size} zones hold buildings")

    STARR export¶

    calculate_starr_inventory assembles the STARR table; save_starr_inputs writes it together with Wind_Tr.npy, Flood_Tr.npy, Hurricane_name.npy and a metadata file. The rows of the CSV and of the arrays align, which the reload below verifies.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    if data_available:
    exposure.starr_inventory = exposure.calculate_starr_inventory(exposure.clipped_inventory, exposure.zone_ids)
    export_paths = exposure.save_starr_inputs(str(output_path / "starr"))
    reloaded_table = pd.read_csv(export_paths["inventory_csv"])
    reloaded_wind = np.load(export_paths["wind_ids"], mmap_mode="r")
    reloaded_names = np.load(export_paths["event_names"])
    assert len(reloaded_table) == reloaded_wind.shape[0]
    assert list(reloaded_names) == exposure.event_names
    assert list(reloaded_table.columns[:4]) == ["building_ID", "t", "YearBuilt", "YearBuiltGroup"]
    print(json.dumps(export_paths, indent=2))
    display(reloaded_table.head())

    Results, pitfalls, and next steps¶

    • The export under Outputs/exposure_workflow/starr/ is the input of the loss-estimation workflow; LossEstimation.load_from_exposure(exposure) hands the same tables over in memory.
    • C is drawn from a seeded stream, so the archetype table differs row by row from the frozen 07/07/2026 Eastern North Carolina export by design; the marginal distributions are the same.
    • The building-type and occupancy filters are off by default, as in the verified run; set DROP_UNMATCHED_OCCUPANCY = True to keep only wood-frame single-family residences.
    • Hazard columns are selected by name (Wind, Flood) and all event files must share the same control points; a mismatch raises ValueError in load_hazard_events.
